title: Legal Matter Triage: Routing Work to the Right Attorney
summary: Learn how General Legal's legal triage process matches every matter with the right lawyer to deliver faster, high-quality legal services.
body_markdown:
Every matter that comes through our door starts with one unglamorous step: triage. Before anyone drafts a clause or rejects the opposing counsel's redlines, someone has to look at the incoming request, figure out what it actually is, and route it to the right attorney.


It's the legal equivalent of an emergency room intake. Diagnose the matter, gauge its urgency, send it to the person best equipped to handle it.


## Key Takeaways


- Every matter starts with **triage** : diagnosing what the request is, gauging its urgency, and routing it to the right attorney, like an **emergency-room intake** .
- Good triage weighs **two things at once** : the nature of the request (practice area, complexity, urgency) and the attorney fit (expertise, bandwidth, availability).
- **Routing right the first time is what makes the firm's speed and quality guarantees hold** , since a misrouted matter has to be reassigned, reviewed, and explained again while the clock runs.
- Triage also serves a **second audience, the attorneys** , matching people to work that fits so specialists are not starved, and the available are not burned out.


## What good triage actually weighs?


Done well, triage looks at two things at once.


- First, the nature of the request. What practice area does it touch? How complex is it? How quickly does the client need it?
- Second, the attorney on the other end. Who has the relevant expertise? Who has the bandwidth this week? Who's available right now? Matching those two columns is the whole game.


Triage weighs the request against attorney fit, then routes to the right desk.


Efficient triage is what makes everything else we promise possible. Our turnaround times and quality guarantees only hold if matters land on the right desk (or, to be more pricise, in the right Slack DMs) the first time.


A misrouted matter is slow, and worse, it has to be reassigned, reviewed again, and explained again. Triage that takes too long is its own failure, because the clock starts the moment the client hits send, not the moment we figure out who's handling it.


## The second audience: the attorneys themselves


But there's a second audience for good triage that's easy to overlook. The attorneys themselves. A routing process that ignores how its lawyers actually work, that overloads the available and starves the specialists, quietly burns people out.


So we listen. We ask attorneys what kinds of matters energize them, where their real expertise lies, and what their week actually looks like. Triage that respects that feedback isn't just more accurate. It's part of what makes General Legal a place attorneys want to stay.


That's the balance we build for. The client gets the right attorney, fast. The attorney gets work that fits. And the firm gets a process that scales without breaking either promise.


## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)


### What is legal matter triage?


Triage is the first step in handling a legal request: looking at what comes in, diagnosing what it actually is, gauging its urgency, and routing it to the attorney best equipped to handle it. It works like emergency-room intake for legal work.


### How does General Legal decide which attorney handles a matter?


By weighing two things at once: the nature of the request (practice area, complexity, how fast the client needs it) and the attorney on the other end (relevant expertise, current bandwidth, and availability right now).


### Why does triage speed matter so much?


Because the clock starts the moment a client hits send, not when the firm figures out who is handling it. Slow or wrong routing means a matter has to be reassigned, reviewed again, and explained again, which erodes the turnaround and quality the firm promises.


### How does triage affect the attorneys, not just clients?


A routing process that overloads the available and starves the specialists quietly burns people out. General Legal asks attorneys what work energizes them, where their expertise lies, and what their week looks like, so matters are matched to fit. That accuracy is also part of what makes it a place attorneys want to stay.


### What happens when a matter is misrouted?


It slows down and has to be reassigned, reviewed, and explained a second time, adding delay on a clock that is already running for the client.
